description: The line plot illustrates the performance of two methods—“ST-ES” and “Random”—in terms of minFDE₂₀ (↓), a trajectory prediction metric where lower values indicate better performance, as the number of in-context examples increases from 0 to 8. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Examples,” is linear and spans integer values from 0 to 8, with tick marks at each integer. The y-axis, labeled “minFDE₂₀ (↓),” is linear and ranges from approximately 0.205 to 0.245, with major tick marks at intervals of 0.01. The “ST-ES” method is represented by a blue line with circular markers and a solid line style; it begins at approximately 0.244 at 0 examples, drops sharply to 0.211 at 1 example, then fluctuates slightly between 0.208 and 0.213 across examples 2 through 8, ending at 0.213 at 8 examples. The “Random” method is shown as an orange line with circular markers and a solid line style; it starts at 0.227 at 0 examples, dips to 0.218 at 1 example, then remains relatively stable with minor fluctuations between 0.217 and 0.224, ending at 0.225 at 8 examples. Both lines show initial improvement with the first example, but ST-ES consistently achieves lower minFDE₂₀ values than Random across all example counts.
